explanation: Life's brevity - time flashes like a horse glimpsed through a wall crack.

history.origin: From "Zhuangzi · Autumn Floods" (《庄子·秋水》). The philosopher Zhuangzi used this metaphor to describe the swift passage of time.
history.story: Zhuangzi observed that life passes as quickly as a white colt glimpsed through a crack in a wall — you see it for an instant, and it is gone. This image became one of Chinese literature's most famous metaphors for the brevity of human existence.

characters.mnemonics: A bright sun (日) shining on fresh snow — everything becomes white and clear.
characters.example_in_context: In "白驹过隙", 白 (bái) contributes to: White colt passes crack.

characters.mnemonics: 马 (horse) + 句 (sentence) — a young horse still learning to run.
characters.example_in_context: In "白驹过隙", 驹 (jū) contributes to: White colt passes crack.

characters.mnemonics: 辶 (walk) + 寸 (inch) — even an inch of walking means passing through.
characters.example_in_context: In "白驹过隙", 过 (guò) contributes to: White colt passes crack.

characters.mnemonics: 阝(mound) + 日(sun) + 小(small) — a small gap where sunlight peeks through.
characters.example_in_context: In "白驹过隙", 隙 (xì) contributes to: White colt passes crack.

examples.zh: 人生百年如白驹过隙，青春时光尤其珍贵，不可虚度。
examples.pinyin: Rénshēng bǎi nián rú bái jū guò xì, qīngchūn shíguāng yóuqí zhēnguì, bù kě xūdù.
examples.en: A hundred years of life flash by like a white colt through a crack — youth is especially precious.

examples.zh: 时光如白驹过隙，转眼间我们已从少年变成了中年人。
examples.pinyin: Shíguāng rú bái jū guò xì, zhuǎnyǎn jiān wǒmen yǐ cóng shàonián biànchéng le zhōngnián rén.
examples.en: Time flies like a white colt through a crack — before we know it, we've changed from youths to middle-aged.

explanation: Persevering through hardship by recalling one's original purpose.

history.origin: From Buddhist and Confucian traditions. The phrase gained modern prominence through political and cultural discourse.
history.story: The concept reminds us to preserve the original aspiration we had when we first embarked on a journey. Like a monk who first enters the temple with pure devotion, we must not forget that beginner's mind even as we face worldly temptations.

characters.mnemonics: A simple negation — imagine a hand waving "no."
characters.example_in_context: In "不忘初心", 不 (bù) contributes to: Don't forget beginner's heart.

characters.mnemonics: 亡 (lost) + 心 (heart) — when something is lost from the heart, you forget.
characters.example_in_context: In "不忘初心", 忘 (wàng) contributes to: Don't forget beginner's heart.

characters.mnemonics: 衣 (clothes) + 刀 (knife) — the first cut when making clothes.
characters.example_in_context: In "不忘初心", 初 (chū) contributes to: Don't forget beginner's heart.

characters.mnemonics: A pictograph of the heart — the center of feelings and thought.
characters.example_in_context: In "不忘初心", 心 (xīn) contributes to: Don't forget beginner's heart.

examples.zh: 创业十年，他始终不忘初心，坚持为用户创造价值的理念。
examples.pinyin: Chuàngyè shí nián, tā shǐzhōng bù wàng chū xīn, jiānchí wèi yònghù chuàngzào jiàzhí de lǐniàn.
examples.en: After ten years of entrepreneurship, he never forgets his original aspiration.

examples.zh: 不忘初心，方得始终，只有坚守最初的想法才能走得更远。
examples.pinyin: Bù wàng chū xīn, fāng dé shǐzhōng, zhǐyǒu jiānshǒu zuìchū de xiǎngfǎ cái néng zǒu de gèng yuǎn.
examples.en: Do not forget the beginner's mind — only by holding fast to your original idea can you go further.

explanation: State beyond immortality where time collapses into presence.

history.origin: From Laozi's "Dao De Jing" (《道德经》). One of the core concepts of Daoist philosophy.
history.story: Laozi taught that those who understand the Dao can achieve a long life and clear vision. The phrase embodies the Daoist ideal of harmony with nature leading to longevity and spiritual clarity.

characters.mnemonics: A person with long hair flowing down — representing length and growth.
characters.example_in_context: In "长生久视", 长 (cháng) contributes to: Long life eternal vision.

characters.mnemonics: A sprout growing from the earth — life emerging.
characters.example_in_context: In "长生久视", 生 (shēng) contributes to: Long life eternal vision.

characters.mnemonics: A person leaning on a cane, waiting a long time.
characters.example_in_context: In "长生久视", 久 (jiǔ) contributes to: Long life eternal vision.

characters.mnemonics: 礻(spirit) + 见 (see) — to see with spiritual insight.
characters.example_in_context: In "长生久视", 视 (shì) contributes to: Long life eternal vision.

examples.zh: 道家追求长生久视，通过修炼达到延长寿命的目的。
examples.pinyin: Dàojiā zhuīqiú cháng shēng jiǔ shì, tōngguò xiūliàn dádào yáncháng shòumìng de mùdì.
examples.en: Daoists pursue longevity and lasting vision — through cultivation achieving the goal of extending life.

examples.zh: 长生久视不仅是肉体的延续，更是精神的长存。
examples.pinyin: Cháng shēng jiǔ shì bùjǐn shì ròutǐ de yánxù, gèng shì jīngshén de chángcún.
examples.en: Longevity and lasting vision is not just physical continuation, but spiritual permanence.

explanation: Earthly ties preventing cultivation transcendence.

history.origin: From Buddhist philosophy. "Dust" (尘) represents worldly attachments.
history.story: In Buddhist teaching, our connections to the material world are like dust that settles on the soul. When these karmic ties remain unfulfilled, we cannot achieve liberation. The phrase describes someone still entangled in worldly affairs.

characters.mnemonics: 小 (small) + 土 (earth) — tiny particles of earth.
characters.example_in_context: In "尘缘未了", 尘 (chén) contributes to: Mortal karma unfinished.

characters.mnemonics: 纟(silk) + 豕 (pig) — the threads of fate connecting beings.
characters.example_in_context: In "尘缘未了", 缘 (yuán) contributes to: Mortal karma unfinished.

characters.mnemonics: 木 (tree) with a branch that hasn't fully grown — not yet.
characters.example_in_context: In "尘缘未了", 未 (wèi) contributes to: Mortal karma unfinished.

characters.mnemonics: A simple hook shape — completion.
characters.example_in_context: In "尘缘未了", 了 (liǎo) contributes to: Mortal karma unfinished.

examples.zh: 他虽然出家修行，但尘缘未了，心中仍挂念着年迈的母亲。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán chūjiā xiūxíng, dàn chén yuán wèi liǎo, xīn zhōng réng guàniàn zhe niánmài de mǔqīn.
examples.en: Though he became a monk, worldly ties remain unended — his heart still worries about his elderly mother.

examples.zh: 尘缘未了的人，难以真正放下世俗的牵挂和欲望。
examples.pinyin: Chén yuán wèi liǎo de rén, nányǐ zhēnzhèng fàngxià shìsú de qiāguà hé yùwàng.
examples.en: Those with unfinished worldly ties find it hard to truly let go of secular attachments and desires.

explanation: The spiritual journey beyond mortal limitations.

history.origin: From Confucian philosophy, describing the highest level of moral cultivation.
history.story: Confucius and his disciples described a path of self-cultivation: from ordinary person to noble person to sage. This phrase marks the ultimate achievement — transcending the mundane to reach sainthood.

characters.mnemonics: 走 (walk) + 召 (call) — to run ahead, to surpass.
characters.example_in_context: In "超凡入圣", 超 (chāo) contributes to: Transcend ordinary, enter sagehood.

characters.mnemonics: 几 (table) with a dot — something common, ordinary.
characters.example_in_context: In "超凡入圣", 凡 (fán) contributes to: Transcend ordinary, enter sagehood.

characters.mnemonics: Two strokes converging inward — entering.
characters.example_in_context: In "超凡入圣", 入 (rù) contributes to: Transcend ordinary, enter sagehood.

characters.mnemonics: 又 (again) + 土 (earth) — the highest attainment on earth.
characters.example_in_context: In "超凡入圣", 圣 (shèng) contributes to: Transcend ordinary, enter sagehood.

examples.zh: 他多年苦心修行，终于超凡入圣，成为一代武学宗师。
examples.pinyin: Tā duō nián kǔxīn xiūxíng, zhōngyú chāo fán rù shèng, chéngwéi yī dài wǔxué zōngshī.
examples.en: After years of devoted practice, he transcended the ordinary and entered sagehood.

examples.zh: 读书不是为了炫耀知识，而是为了超凡入圣，提升人格。
examples.pinyin: Dúshū bùshì wéile xuànyào zhīshi, érshì wéile chāo fán rù shèng, tíshēng réngé.
examples.en: Reading is not for showing off knowledge, but to transcend the ordinary and elevate one's character.

explanation: Patient cultivation yielding eventual results.

history.origin: From ancient Chinese agricultural wisdom, elevated to philosophical metaphor.
history.story: In nature, flowers bloom in spring and fruits ripen in autumn — there is always a cause-and-effect relationship. Similarly, a person's achievements are the result of earlier efforts and cultivation.

characters.mnemonics: 三 (three) + 人 (person) + 日 (sun) — three people under the spring sun.
characters.example_in_context: In "春华秋实", 春 (chūn) contributes to: Spring bloom autumn fruit.

characters.mnemonics: 花 (flower) — splendor, flourishing beauty.
characters.example_in_context: In "春华秋实", 华 (huá) contributes to: Spring bloom autumn fruit.

characters.mnemonics: 禾 (grain) + 火 (fire) — the burning colors of autumn.
characters.example_in_context: In "春华秋实", 秋 (qiū) contributes to: Spring bloom autumn fruit.

characters.example_in_context: In "春华秋实", 实 (shí) contributes to: Spring bloom autumn fruit.

examples.zh: 年轻人应该趁时光正好，努力学习，春华秋实，丰收在望。
examples.pinyin: Niánqīng rén yīnggāi chèn shíguāng zhèng hǎo, nǔlì xuéxí, chūn huá qiū shí, fēngshōu zài wàng.
examples.en: Young people should seize the good time to study — spring blossoms, autumn fruits; a bountiful harvest awaits.

examples.zh: 春华秋实，没有春天的播种就没有秋天的收获。
examples.pinyin: Chūn huá qiū shí, méiyǒu chūntiān de bōzhǒng jiù méiyǒu qiūtiān de shōuhuò.
examples.en: Spring blossoms and autumn fruits — without spring planting, there is no autumn harvest.

english_similar.idiom: Great oaks from little acorns grow

explanation: Equanimity in facing praise and slander alike.

history.origin: From Laozi's "Dao De Jing" (《道德经》). A core concept of Daoist equanimity.
history.story: Laozi taught: "Can you remain centered between favor and disgrace?" The sage who achieves this state is not elated by praise nor devastated by criticism — they maintain inner peace regardless of external circumstances.

characters.mnemonics: 宀 (roof) + 龙 (dragon) — a dragon kept under the roof, favored.
characters.example_in_context: In "宠辱不惊", 宠 (chǒng) contributes to: Unmoved by favor or disgrace.

characters.mnemonics: 辰 (time) + 寸 (inch) — measuring smallness, humiliation.
characters.example_in_context: In "宠辱不惊", 辱 (rǔ) contributes to: Unmoved by favor or disgrace.

characters.example_in_context: In "宠辱不惊", 不 (bù) contributes to: Unmoved by favor or disgrace.

characters.mnemonics: 忄(heart) + 京 (capital) — the heart races.
characters.example_in_context: In "宠辱不惊", 惊 (jīng) contributes to: Unmoved by favor or disgrace.

examples.zh: 面对成败都能宠辱不惊，这是一种难得的修养和定力。
examples.pinyin: Miàn duì chéngbài dōu néng chǒng rǔ bù jīng, zhè shì yī zhǒng nándé de xiūyǎng hé dìnglì.
examples.en: Being unmoved by both success and disgrace is a rare cultivation and composure.

examples.zh: 他身居高位却宠辱不惊，始终保持谦逊低调的作风。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēn jū gāowèi què chǒng rǔ bù jīng, shǐzhōng bǎochí qiānxùn dīdiào de zuòfēng.
examples.en: Though holding a high position, he is unmoved by favor or disgrace.

explanation: Cultivation process of destroying illusions to embody pure reality.

history.origin: Cultivation process of destroying illusions to embody pure reality.

characters.mnemonics: 斤 (axe) cutting through — to sever.
characters.example_in_context: In "断惑证真", 断 (duàn) contributes to: Sever delusion, verify truth.

characters.mnemonics: 或 (perhaps) + 心 (heart) — the heart is uncertain.
characters.example_in_context: In "断惑证真", 惑 (huò) contributes to: Sever delusion, verify truth.

characters.mnemonics: 讠(speech) + 正 (correct) — speaking what is right.
characters.example_in_context: In "断惑证真", 证 (zhèng) contributes to: Sever delusion, verify truth.

characters.example_in_context: In "断惑证真", 真 (zhēn) contributes to: Sever delusion, verify truth.

examples.zh: 通过长期禅修，他终于断惑证真，明白了宇宙人生的真相。
examples.pinyin: Tōngguò chángcóng chánxiū, tā zhōngyú duàn huò zhèng zhēn, míngbái le yǔzhòu rénshēng de zhēnxiàng.
examples.en: Through long-term Zen practice, he finally dispelled doubts and proved the truth.

examples.zh: 断惑证真是修行的必经之路，只有破除迷惑才能见性。
examples.pinyin: Duàn huò zhèng zhēn shì xiūxíng de bìjīng zhī lù, zhǐyǒu pòchú míhuò cái néng jiàn xìng.
examples.en: Dispelling doubts and proving truth is a necessary part of spiritual cultivation.

english_similar.idiom: Separate the wheat from the chaff

explanation: The deepest truths are found in simplicity, not complexity.

history.origin: Daoist philosophical principle about the nature of truth and wisdom.
history.story: The greatest truths are often the simplest. Complex theories and elaborate rituals miss the point — the Dao (the Way) is found in simplicity, in the natural order of things, not in artificial complexity.

characters.mnemonics: A person with arms spread wide — bigness, grandeur.
characters.example_in_context: In "大道至简", 大 (dà) contributes to: Great Dao is supremely simple.

characters.mnemonics: 首 (head) + 辶 (walk) — leading with the head, walking the Way.
characters.example_in_context: In "大道至简", 道 (dào) contributes to: Great Dao is supremely simple.

characters.mnemonics: Arriving at the destination — the ultimate.
characters.example_in_context: In "大道至简", 至 (zhì) contributes to: Great Dao is supremely simple.

characters.mnemonics: 竹 (bamboo) + 间 (between) — bamboo strips for simple writing.
characters.example_in_context: In "大道至简", 简 (jiǎn) contributes to: Great Dao is supremely simple.

examples.zh: 真正有效的营销策略大道至简，去掉噱头直击用户痛点。
examples.pinyin: Zhēnzhèng yǒuxiào de yíngxiāo cèlüè dà dào zhì jiǎn, qùdiào xuétou zhí jī yònghù tòngdiǎn.
examples.en: A truly effective marketing strategy is supremely simple — cut gimmicks and hit the user's pain point directly.

examples.zh: 越是复杂的科学理论，大道至简，往往能用一句话概括本质。
examples.pinyin: Yuè shì fùzá de kēxué lǐlùn, dà dào zhì jiǎn, wǎngwǎng néng yòng yī jù huà gàikuò běnzhì.
examples.en: The more complex a scientific theory, the more supremely simple it tends to be.

explanation: True sages appear simple-minded to the unenlightened.

history.origin: From Laozi's "Dao De Jing" (《道德经》). A paradox at the heart of Daoist wisdom.
history.story: The truly wise person appears foolish to the unwise. They do not boast of their knowledge or seek to impress. Like the uncarved block, they retain their natural simplicity, which is the highest form of wisdom.

characters.mnemonics: A person with arms spread wide — bigness, grandeur.
characters.example_in_context: In "大智若愚", 大 (dà) contributes to: Great wisdom seems foolish.

characters.mnemonics: 知 (know) + 日 (day) — knowing day by day, gaining wisdom.

characters.example_in_context: In "大智若愚", 若 (ruò) contributes to: Great wisdom seems foolish.

characters.example_in_context: In "大智若愚", 愚 (yú) contributes to: Great wisdom seems foolish.

examples.zh: 他看起来像普通农民，其实大智若愚，掌握了精湛医术。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlái xiàng pǔtōng nóngmín, qíshí dà zhì ruò yú, zhǎngwò le jīngzhàn yīshù.
examples.en: He looks like an ordinary farmer, but great wisdom seems foolish — he actually masters exquisite medical skills.

examples.zh: 真正有智慧的人往往大智若愚，不轻易炫耀自己的才华。
examples.pinyin: Zhēnzhèng yǒu zhìhuì de rén wǎngwǎng dà zhì ruò yú, bù qīngyì xuànyào zìjǐ de cáihuá.
examples.en: Truly wise people often appear foolish — they don't readily show off their talents.

explanation: Universal principles mirror organic cosmic patterns.

history.origin: From Laozi's "Dao De Jing" (《道德经》). The fundamental principle of Daoism.
history.story: "The Dao follows its own nature." Nature is the highest authority. The Dao does not impose itself on things but allows them to follow their own way. This is the essence of wu wei — working with the natural flow, not against it.

characters.mnemonics: 首 (head) + 辶 (walk) — leading with the head, walking the Way.
characters.example_in_context: In "道法自然", 道 (dào) contributes to: Dao follows nature.

characters.example_in_context: In "道法自然", 法 (fǎ) contributes to: Dao follows nature.

characters.example_in_context: In "道法自然", 然 (rán) contributes to: Dao follows nature.

examples.zh: 城市规划应当道法自然，尊重原有的地形和水系。
examples.pinyin: Chéngshì guīhuà yīngdāng dào fǎ zì rán, zūnzhòng yuányǒu de dìxíng hé shuǐxì.
examples.en: City planning should follow natural law — respecting original terrain and water systems.

examples.zh: 道法自然，万物都有其运行的规律，不需要强行干预。
examples.pinyin: Dào fǎ zì rán, wànwù dōu yǒu qí yùnxíng de guīlǜ, bù xūyào qiángxíng gānyù.
examples.en: The Dao follows nature — all things have their patterns; there is no need for forced intervention.

explanation: Truths inexplicable to the unawakened - nearly biologically obvious.

history.origin: From Daoist philosophical texts, describing the hidden nature of the Dao.
history.story: The Dao is hidden in the deepest mysteries, beyond the reach of ordinary understanding. It cannot be seen or grasped directly — only through quiet contemplation can one begin to perceive its depths.

characters.mnemonics: 首 (head) + 辶 (walk) — leading with the head, walking the Way.
characters.example_in_context: In "道隐奥赜", 道 (dào) contributes to: Dao hidden profound mysteries.

characters.mnemonics: 阝(mound) + 急 (urgent) — hiding behind a mound.
characters.example_in_context: In "道隐奥赜", 隐 (yǐn) contributes to: Dao hidden profound mysteries.

characters.mnemonics: 屋里藏着 treasure — something deep and mysterious.
characters.example_in_context: In "道隐奥赜", 奥 (ào) contributes to: Dao hidden profound mysteries.

characters.example_in_context: In "道隐奥赜", 赜 (zé) contributes to: Dao hidden profound mysteries.

examples.zh: 道隐奥赜，真正的道总是隐藏在最深的地方，不易被发现。
examples.pinyin: Dào yǐn ào zé, zhēnzhèng de dào zǒngshì yǐncáng zài zuì shēn de dìfāng, bù yì bèi fāxiàn.
examples.en: The Dao hides in profound depths — the true Dao is concealed in the deepest places.

examples.zh: 道隐奥赜，大道至简却难以领悟，需要用心体悟。
examples.pinyin: Dào yǐn ào zé, dà dào zhì jiǎn què nányǐ lǐngwù, xūyào yòng xīn tǐ wù.
examples.en: The Dao hides in profound depths — supremely simple yet difficult to comprehend.

english_similar.idiom: There's more than meets the eye

explanation: Alignment with cosmic principles attracts serendipity.

history.origin: From Mencius (《孟子》). A principle of righteous governance.
history.story: Mencius taught that the ruler who follows the Dao will receive help from many. Conversely, the tyrant who abandons the Dao will find himself abandoned. Moral authority attracts allies naturally.

characters.mnemonics: 彳(walk) + 日 (sun) + 寸 (inch) — gaining step by step.
characters.example_in_context: In "得道多助", 得 (dé) contributes to: Attain Dao, receive much help.

examples.zh: 得道多助，失道寡助，正义的事业总会得到支持。
examples.pinyin: Dé dào duō zhù, shī dào guǎ zhù, zhèngyì de shìyè zǒng huì dédào zhīchí.
examples.en: Those who have the Dao get much help; those who lose it get little — the cause of justice always receives support.

examples.zh: 一个企业的价值观正确，就能得道多助，吸引优秀人才。
examples.pinyin: Yī gè qǐyè de jiàzhíguān zhèngquè, jiù néng dé dào duō zhù, xīyǐn yōuxiù réncái.
examples.en: When a company's values are correct, it gains much support and attracts excellent talent.

examples.zh: 那个山洞里的老者说，洞中方七日，世上已千年，时间感受因境而异。
examples.pinyin: Nàge shāndòng lǐ de lǎozhě shuō, dòng zhōng fāng qī rì, shì shàng yǐ qiān nián, shíjiān gǎnshòu yīn jìng ér yì.
examples.en: The old man in the cave said: seven days in the cave, a thousand years in the world — time perception differs by realm.

examples.zh: 神话中的仙人常有这样的经历，洞中方七日，世上已千年。
examples.pinyin: Shénhuà zhōng de xiānrén cháng yǒu zhèyàng de jīnglì, dòng zhōng fāng qī rì, shì shàng yǐ qiān nián.
examples.en: Immortals in mythology often have this experience — seven days in the cave, a thousand years in the world.

english_similar.idiom: A day is like a thousand years

explanation: Exceptional insight to perceive deeper realities.

history.origin: From Buddhist-influenced Chinese philosophy about insight.
history.story: Most people see the surface of things. But the person with the eye of wisdom sees the true nature beneath — impermanence, interdependence, and the void. This unique perception allows them to understand what others miss.

characters.mnemonics: 犭(dog) + 虫 (insect) — alone, solitary.
characters.example_in_context: In "独具慧眼", 独 (dú) contributes to: Alone possess wise eyes.

characters.example_in_context: In "独具慧眼", 具 (jù) contributes to: Alone possess wise eyes.

characters.mnemonics: 目 (eye) + 艮 (tough) — the eye that sees truly.
characters.example_in_context: In "独具慧眼", 眼 (yǎn) contributes to: Alone possess wise eyes.

examples.zh: 在众人还在观望时，他独具慧眼，率先投资了这个项目。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhòngrén hái zài guānwàng shí, tā dú jù huì yǎn, shuàixiān tóuzī le zhège xiàngmù.
examples.en: While everyone else was hesitating, he uniquely possessed wise eyes — being first to invest.

examples.zh: 独具慧眼的收藏家在一堆旧货中发现了价值连城的宝物。
examples.pinyin: Dú jù huì yǎn de shōucángjiā zài yī duī jiùhuò zhōng fāxiàn le jiàzhí liánchéng de bǎowù.
examples.en: A collector with uniquely wise eyes discovered a treasure of immeasurable value.

explanation: Seeing a universe within the smallest phenomenon.

history.origin: From Buddhist scripture about the Buddha's microscopic vision.
history.story: Legend says the Buddha could look at a bowl of water and see millions of living beings — the truth that even a drop of water contains countless forms of life. This illustrates the Buddhist teaching of interconnectedness.

characters.mnemonics: 亻(person) + 弓 (bow) — one who has overcome attachments.
characters.example_in_context: In "佛观一钵水", 佛 (fó) contributes to: Buddha observes bowl of water.

characters.example_in_context: In "佛观一钵水", 观 (guān) contributes to: Buddha observes bowl of water.

characters.example_in_context: In "佛观一钵水", 一 (yī) contributes to: Buddha observes bowl of water.

characters.example_in_context: In "佛观一钵水", 钵 (bō) contributes to: Buddha observes bowl of water.

characters.example_in_context: In "佛观一钵水", 水 (shuǐ) contributes to: Buddha observes bowl of water.

examples.zh: 佛观一钵水，发现里面有八万四千虫，众生皆平等。
examples.pinyin: Fó guān yī bō shuǐ, fāxiàn lǐmiàn yǒu bā wàn sì qiān chóng, zhòngshēng jiē píngděng.
examples.en: The Buddha observed a bowl of water and discovered eighty-four thousand creatures — all beings are equal.

examples.zh: 佛观一钵水，提醒我们微观世界里也充满生命，要以慈悲心对待。
examples.pinyin: Fó guān yī bō shuǐ, tíxǐng wǒmen wēiguān shìjiè lǐ yě chōngmǎn shēngmìng, yào yǐ cíbēi xīn duìdài.
examples.en: The Buddha viewing a bowl of water reminds us the microscopic world is full of life.

english_similar.idiom: A world in a grain of sand

explanation: Balancing material well-being with spiritual insight.

history.origin: From Mahayana Buddhism. Essential for the bodhisattva path.
history.story: The path to enlightenment requires both merit (福) and wisdom (慧). Accumulating merit through good deeds and cultivating wisdom through meditation are equally important — neither alone is sufficient.

characters.mnemonics: 礻(spirit) + 畐 (abundance) — divine abundance.
characters.example_in_context: In "福慧双修", 福 (fú) contributes to: Cultivate fortune and wisdom together.

characters.mnemonics: 彗 (comet) + 心 (heart) — a heart that shines like a comet.

characters.example_in_context: In "福慧双修", 修 (xiū) contributes to: Cultivate fortune and wisdom together.

examples.zh: 学佛之人追求福慧双修，既要积德行善，也要开启智慧。
examples.pinyin: Xué fó zhī rén zhuīqiú fú huì shuāng xiū, jì yào jī dé xíngshàn, yě yào kāiqǐ zhìhuì.
examples.en: Buddhist practitioners pursue cultivating both fortune and wisdom.

examples.zh: 福慧双修的人生最圆满，既有物质幸福，也有精神富足。
examples.pinyin: Fú huì shuāng xiū de rénshēng zuì yuánmǎn, jì yǒu wùzhì xìngfú, yě yǒu jīngshén fùzú.
examples.en: A life of cultivating both fortune and wisdom is most complete.

explanation: Mortal existence perceived as illusory by awakened cultivators.

history.origin: From the "Zhuangzi" and Li Bai's famous prose.
history.story: Zhuangzi dreamed he was a butterfly, and upon waking couldn't tell if he was a man who dreamed of being a butterfly, or a butterfly dreaming of being a man. Li Bai later wrote: "Life is like a dream, how much joy can there be?"

characters.mnemonics: 氵(water) + 子 (child) — a child floating on water, impermanent.
characters.example_in_context: In "浮生若梦", 浮 (fú) contributes to: Floating life like dream.

characters.mnemonics: A sprout growing from the earth — life emerging.

characters.mnemonics: 林 (forest) + 夕 (evening) — seeing forests in the evening, dreaming.
characters.example_in_context: In "浮生若梦", 梦 (mèng) contributes to: Floating life like dream.

examples.zh: 回首往事，浮生若梦，我们走过的岁月如同一场梦。
examples.pinyin: Huí shǒu wǎngshì, fú shēng ruò mèng, wǒmen zǒuguò de suìyuè rú tóng yī chǎng mèng.
examples.en: Looking back, this floating life is like a dream — the years we've walked through are like a dream.

examples.zh: 浮生若梦，我们应当珍惜当下，不要虚度光阴。
examples.pinyin: Fú shēng ruò mèng, wǒmen yīngdāng zhēnxī dāngxià, bùyào xūdù guāngyīn.
examples.en: This floating life is like a dream — we should cherish the present and not waste time.

explanation: True detachment leaves no spiritual residue.

history.origin: From Chan Buddhist philosophy about impermanence.
history.story: When wind passes through the forest, it moves the leaves, but leaves no trace behind. This is a metaphor for the enlightened mind — engaging with the world without leaving karmic imprints.

characters.mnemonics: Wind blowing through — movement, style.
characters.example_in_context: In "风过无痕", 风 (fēng) contributes to: Wind passes without trace.

characters.mnemonics: 辶 (walk) + 寸 (inch) — even an inch of walking means passing through.
characters.example_in_context: In "风过无痕", 过 (guò) contributes to: Wind passes without trace.

characters.mnemonics: Without, nothingness.
characters.example_in_context: In "风过无痕", 无 (wú) contributes to: Wind passes without trace.

examples.zh: 他一生做好事无数，却风过无痕，从不求回报。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī shēng zuò hǎoshì wúshù, què fēng guò wú hén, cóng bù qiú huíbào.
examples.en: He did countless good deeds all his life, yet wind passes without leaving marks — never seeking reward.

examples.zh: 真正的善行应该风过无痕，不要带着功利心去做。
examples.pinyin: Zhēnzhèng de shànxíng yīnggāi fēng guò wú hén, bùyào dài zhe gōnglì xīn qù zuò.
examples.en: True virtuous action should be like wind passing without traces — don't act with an ulterior motive.

explanation: Transcending spiritual methods after achieving enlightenment.

history.origin: From the Diamond Sutra (《金刚经》).
history.story: The Buddha compared his teachings to a raft used to cross a river. Once you reach the other shore, you don't carry the raft on your back. Similarly, even the Dharma should be abandoned once it has served its purpose.

characters.mnemonics: 氵(water) + 去 (go) — water flows according to law.
characters.example_in_context: In "法尚应舍", 法 (fǎ) contributes to: Even dharma should be abandoned.

characters.mnemonics: 小 (small) + 冋 (border) — still, yet.
characters.example_in_context: In "法尚应舍", 尚 (shàng) contributes to: Even dharma should be abandoned.

characters.mnemonics: 广 (wide) + 鸟 (bird) — responding to nature's call.
characters.example_in_context: In "法尚应舍", 应 (yīng) contributes to: Even dharma should be abandoned.

characters.mnemonics: 人 (person) + 吉 (luck) — letting go to find fortune.
characters.example_in_context: In "法尚应舍", 舍 (shě) contributes to: Even dharma should be abandoned.

examples.zh: 佛教认为法尚应舍，即便是佛法也不能执着。
examples.pinyin: Fójiào rènwéi fǎ shàng yīng shě, jíbiàn shì fófǎ yě bù néng zhízhe.
examples.en: Buddhism teaches even the Dharma should be abandoned — even Buddhist teachings cannot be attached to.

examples.zh: 法尚应舍，何况非法，学会放下才能真正解脱。
examples.pinyin: Fǎ shàng yīng shě, hé kuàng fēi fǎ, xuéhuì fàngxià cái néng zhēnzhèng jiětuō.
examples.en: Even the Dharma should be abandoned, let alone non-Dharma — learning to let go brings true liberation.

explanation: Spiritual awakening through shedding artificial complexity.

history.origin: From Daoist philosophy. The return to original simplicity.
history.story: Like uncarved jade that contains all potential within its raw form, the sage returns to their original nature — free from artificial desires and intellectual complexity. This is the highest state of Daoist cultivation.

characters.mnemonics: 辶(walk) + 反 (reverse) — walking back.
characters.example_in_context: In "返璞归真", 返 (fǎn) contributes to: Return plain, go back true.

characters.mnemonics: 王 (king) + 业 (industry) — uncarved jade, raw beauty.
characters.example_in_context: In "返璞归真", 璞 (pǔ) contributes to: Return plain, go back true.

characters.mnemonics: To return to the source.
characters.example_in_context: In "返璞归真", 归 (guī) contributes to: Return plain, go back true.

characters.mnemonics: 目 (eye) seeing truly — truth, authenticity.
characters.example_in_context: In "返璞归真", 真 (zhēn) contributes to: Return plain, go back true.

examples.zh: 功成名就后，他选择返璞归真，搬回乡下老家生活。
examples.pinyin: Gōng chéng míng jiù hòu, tā xuǎnzé fǎn pǔ guī zhēn, bān huí xiāngxià lǎojiā shēnghuó.
examples.en: After achieving success, he chose to return to plainness, moving back to his countryside hometown.

examples.zh: 这款手机的设计理念是返璞归真，没有多余的APP和广告。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn shǒujī de shèjì lǐniàn shì fǎn pǔ guī zhēn, méiyǒu duōyú de APP hé guǎnggào.
examples.en: This phone's design philosophy is to return to plainness — no extra apps or ads.

explanation: Harmonizing opposing forces like strength and gentleness.

history.origin: From the "I Ching" (《易经》) about balance of opposites.
history.story: The I Ching teaches that the strongest thing combines hardness and softness. Water is soft yet wears away stone. A bamboo bends in the storm but does not break. True strength lies in balance.

characters.mnemonics: 冈 (ridge) + 刂 (knife) — firm as a mountain ridge.
characters.example_in_context: In "刚柔并济", 刚 (gāng) contributes to: Hard and soft combined.

characters.mnemonics: 矛 (spear) + 木 (wood) — wood that bends, flexible yet strong.
characters.example_in_context: In "刚柔并济", 柔 (róu) contributes to: Hard and soft combined.

characters.mnemonics: Two people standing side by side — together.
characters.example_in_context: In "刚柔并济", 并 (bìng) contributes to: Hard and soft combined.

characters.mnemonics: 氵(water) + 齐 (together) — crossing water together, helping.
characters.example_in_context: In "刚柔并济", 济 (jì) contributes to: Hard and soft combined.

examples.zh: 好的领导者懂得刚柔并济，既坚持原则，又灵活变通。
examples.pinyin: Hǎo de lǐngdǎozhě dǒngdé gāng róu bìng jì, jì jiānchí yuánzé, yòu línghuó biàntōng.
examples.en: Good leaders know to combine hardness and softness — adhering to principles while being flexible.

examples.zh: 太极拳讲究刚柔并济，以柔克刚，四两拨千斤。
examples.pinyin: Tàijíquán jiǎngjiū gāng róu bìng jì, yǐ róu kè gāng, sì liǎng bō qiān jīn.
examples.en: Tai Chi emphasizes combining hardness and softness — using softness to overcome hardness.

english_similar.idiom: Walk softly and carry a big stick

explanation: Cutting worldly attachments to achieve ascension.

history.origin: Cutting worldly attachments to achieve ascension.

characters.example_in_context: In "慧剑斩情丝", 慧 (huì) contributes to: Wisdom sword severs emotion threads.

characters.example_in_context: In "慧剑斩情丝", 斩 (zhǎn) contributes to: Wisdom sword severs emotion threads.

examples.zh: 遇到感情纠葛时，需要慧剑斩情丝，果断放下执念。
examples.pinyin: Yùdào gǎnqíng jiūgé shí, xūyào huì jiàn zhǎn qíng sī, guǒduàn fàngxià zhíniàn.
examples.en: When facing emotional entanglement, the wisdom-sword must sever emotion threads.

examples.zh: 修行之人当以慧剑斩情丝，断绝一切烦恼的根源。
examples.pinyin: Xiūxíng zhī rén dāng yǐ huì jiàn zhǎn qíng sī, duànjué yīqiè fá'nǎo de gēnyuán.
examples.en: Those who cultivate should wield the wisdom-sword to sever emotion threads.

explanation: Adversity and blessing are interconnected forces.

history.origin: From Laozi's "Dao De Jing" (《道德经》).
history.story: Laozi said: "Misfortune is what fortune leans upon; fortune is where misfortune hides." The farmer who loses his horse may find a better one. The apparent disaster contains the seed of blessing.

characters.mnemonics: 礻(spirit) + 内 (inside) — disaster from within.
characters.example_in_context: In "祸福相依", 祸 (huò) contributes to: Misfortune and fortune lean together.

characters.mnemonics: 礻(spirit) + 畐 (abundance) — divine abundance.
characters.example_in_context: In "祸福相依", 福 (fú) contributes to: Misfortune and fortune lean together.

characters.mnemonics: 木 (tree) + 目 (eye) — seeing each other.
characters.example_in_context: In "祸福相依", 相 (xiāng) contributes to: Misfortune and fortune lean together.

characters.mnemonics: 亻(person) + 衣 (clothes) — leaning on someone.
characters.example_in_context: In "祸福相依", 依 (yī) contributes to: Misfortune and fortune lean together.

examples.zh: 这次危机让他被裁员，但也是创业的契机，祸福相依。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì wēijī ràng tā bèi cáiyuán, dàn yě shì chuàngyè de qìjī, huò fú xiāng yī.
examples.en: The crisis got him laid off, but it was also his entrepreneurial chance — misfortune and fortune are interdependent.

examples.zh: 祸福相依，经历过困难的人更懂得珍惜幸福。
examples.pinyin: Huò fú xiāng yī, jīnglì guò kùnnán de rén gèng dǒngdé zhēnxī xìngfú.
examples.en: Misfortune and fortune are interdependent — those who have weathered hardship better cherish happiness.

english_similar.idiom: Every cloud has a silver lining

explanation: Moral integrity creates foundations for great achievements.

history.origin: From the "I Ching" (《易经》).
history.story: "The earth's virtue is vast — it carries all things." Just as the earth supports mountains, rivers, and all living things without discrimination, a person of great virtue can bear great responsibilities.

characters.mnemonics: 厂 (cliff) + 日 (sun) + 子 (child) — deep as a cliff.
characters.example_in_context: In "厚德载物", 厚 (hòu) contributes to: Deep virtue carries matter.

characters.mnemonics: 彳(walk) + 十 + 四 + 一 + 心 — walking with heart, virtue.
characters.example_in_context: In "厚德载物", 德 (dé) contributes to: Deep virtue carries matter.

characters.example_in_context: In "厚德载物", 物 (wù) contributes to: Deep virtue carries matter.

examples.zh: 古人云厚德载物，只有品德高尚的人才能承担大任。
examples.pinyin: Gǔrén yún hòu dé zài wù, zhǐyǒu pǐndé gāoshàng de rén cái néng dāndān dà rèn.
examples.en: The ancients said deep virtue carries all things — only people of noble character can bear great responsibility.

examples.zh: 一个企业要想长久发展，必须厚德载物，赢得用户信任。
examples.pinyin: Yī gè qǐyè yào xiǎng chángjiǔ fāzhǎn, bìxū hòu dé zài wù, yíngdé yònghù xìnrèn.
examples.en: For a company to develop sustainably, it must cultivate deep virtue and earn customers' trust.

explanation: Patient accumulation leading to profound breakthroughs.

history.origin: From Su Shi (苏轼), the Song Dynasty poet.
history.story: Su Shi compared scholarly achievement to cooking — slow and steady accumulation produces the best results. Deep preparation leads to effortless output. Rush and shallow effort produce nothing lasting.

characters.mnemonics: 厂 (cliff) + 日 (sun) + 子 (child) — deep as a cliff.
characters.example_in_context: In "厚积薄发", 厚 (hòu) contributes to: Accumulate thickly, release thinly.

characters.mnemonics: 禾 (grain) + 只 (only) — storing grain, accumulating.
characters.example_in_context: In "厚积薄发", 积 (jī) contributes to: Accumulate thickly, release thinly.

examples.pinyin: Tā gōngzī bù gāo, dàn zhī zú cháng lè, zǎo shuì zǎo qǐ, shēnghuó hěn jiànkāng.
examples.en: His salary isn't high, but he knows contentment and is always joyful.

examples.zh: 知足常乐，不要和别人攀比，珍惜已有的就是幸福。
examples.pinyin: Zhī zú cháng lè, bùyào hé biéren pānbǐ, zhēnxī yǒu de jiùshì xìngfú.
examples.en: Know contentment and enjoy lasting happiness — treasuring what you have is true bliss.

english_similar.idiom: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush

explanation: Sacred lands cultivating enlightened beings.

history.origin: From Chinese literary tradition.
history.story: "The spirit of mountains and rivers nurtures outstanding people." The landscape itself cultivates genius. Great scholars and leaders seem to emerge from specific regions.

characters.mnemonics: 钅(metal) + 中 (middle) — a metal bell.
characters.example_in_context: In "钟灵毓秀", 钟 (zhōng) contributes to: Bell essence nourishes beauty.

characters.mnemonics: Spirit moving like fire.
characters.example_in_context: In "钟灵毓秀", 灵 (líng) contributes to: Bell essence nourishes beauty.

characters.mnemonics: Every mother nurturing life.
characters.example_in_context: In "钟灵毓秀", 毓 (yù) contributes to: Bell essence nourishes beauty.

characters.mnemonics: 禾 (grain) + 乃 (then) — grain flowering.
characters.example_in_context: In "钟灵毓秀", 秀 (xiù) contributes to: Bell essence nourishes beauty.

examples.zh: 江南水乡钟灵毓秀，自古以来人才辈出，文风鼎盛。
examples.pinyin: Jiāngnán shuǐxiāng zhōng líng yù xiù, zìgǔ yǐlái réncái bèichū, wénfēng dǐngshèng.
examples.en: Jiangnan water towns are blessed with spirit that nurtures excellence.

examples.zh: 这个地方钟灵毓秀，培养出了许多杰出的科学家和艺术家。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìfāng zhōng líng yù xiù, péiyǎng chū le xǔduō jiéchū de kēxuéjiā hé yìshùjiā.
examples.en: This place is endowed with spiritual beauty that cultivates excellence.

explanation: The endless revolution of cosmic and personal cycles.

history.origin: From the "I Ching" (《易经》).
history.story: "The cycle completes and begins again." Like the seasons, like day and night, all things move in cycles. There is no true ending — only transformation and renewal.

characters.mnemonics: 咼 (mouth) + 冂 (border) — going around completely.
characters.example_in_context: In "周而复始", 周 (zhōu) contributes to: Cycle and restart.

characters.mnemonics: Character: 而
characters.example_in_context: In "周而复始", 而 (ér) contributes to: Cycle and restart.

characters.mnemonics: Character: 复
characters.example_in_context: In "周而复始", 复 (fù) contributes to: Cycle and restart.

characters.mnemonics: 女 (woman) + 台 (platform) — beginning, origin.
characters.example_in_context: In "周而复始", 始 (shǐ) contributes to: Cycle and restart.

examples.zh: 四季更替，周而复始，春天过去又是新的开始。
examples.pinyin: Sìjì gēngtì, zhōu ér fù shǐ, chūntiān guòqù yòu shì xīn de kāishǐ.
examples.en: The seasons change and cycle endlessly — after spring passes, it's a new beginning again.

examples.zh: 历史总是周而复始，提醒我们以史为鉴，不要重蹈覆辙。
examples.pinyin: Lìshǐ zǒng shì zhōu ér fù shǐ, tíxǐng wǒmen yǐ shǐ wéi jiàn, bùyào chóngdǎo fùzhé.
examples.en: History always circles back — reminding us to take history as a lesson.

explanation: Buddhist concept that existence lacks inherent substance.

history.origin: From the Heart Sutra (《心经》).
history.story: "All dharmas are empty." Every phenomenon lacks inherent, independent existence. Things exist only in dependence on causes and conditions. Understanding this is the key to liberation.

characters.mnemonics: 讠(speech) + 者 (person) — all people speaking.
characters.example_in_context: In "诸法皆空", 诸 (zhū) contributes to: All phenomena empty.

characters.mnemonics: 氵(water) + 去 (go) — water flows according to law.
characters.example_in_context: In "诸法皆空", 法 (fǎ) contributes to: All phenomena empty.

characters.mnemonics: 比 (compare) + 白 (white) — all, everyone.
characters.example_in_context: In "诸法皆空", 皆 (jiē) contributes to: All phenomena empty.

characters.mnemonics: 穴 (cave) + 工 (work) — an empty cave.
characters.example_in_context: In "诸法皆空", 空 (kōng) contributes to: All phenomena empty.

examples.zh: 佛教认为诸法皆空，世间一切现象都没有永恒的自性。
examples.pinyin: Fójiào rènwéi zhū fǎ jiē kōng, shìjiān yīqiè xiànxiàng dōu méiyǒu yǒnghéng de zìxìng.
examples.en: Buddhism teaches all phenomena are empty — nothing in the world has eternal self-nature.

examples.zh: 诸法皆空，但修行不能落入顽空，要悲智双运。
examples.pinyin: Zhū fǎ jiē kōng, dàn xiūxíng bù néng luòrù wánkōng, yào bēi zhì shuāng yùn.
examples.en: All phenomena are empty, but cultivation shouldn't fall into nihilistic emptiness.

explanation: Unconscious self-creation of spiritual obstacles.

history.origin: From Chinese proverbial wisdom.
history.story: The silkworm spins its own cocoon and is trapped within it. Similarly, we create our own prisons through our habits, attachments, and patterns of thought.

characters.mnemonics: 亻(person) + 乍 (suddenly) — doing something suddenly.
characters.example_in_context: In "作茧自缚", 作 (zuò) contributes to: Build cocoon self-bound.

characters.mnemonics: 艹 (grass) + 内 (inside) — something wrapped inside.
characters.example_in_context: In "作茧自缚", 茧 (jiǎn) contributes to: Build cocoon self-bound.

characters.mnemonics: A nose pointing at oneself — self.
characters.example_in_context: In "作茧自缚", 自 (zì) contributes to: Build cocoon self-bound.

related_words.meaning: to spin a cocoon around oneself

characters.mnemonics: 纟(silk) + 甫 (beginning) — binding with silk threads.
characters.example_in_context: In "作茧自缚", 缚 (fù) contributes to: Build cocoon self-bound.

examples.zh: 执着于名利的追求，最终只会作茧自缚，困住自己。
examples.pinyin: Zhízhe yú mínglì de zhuīqiú, zuìzhōng zhǐ huì zuò jiǎn zì fù, kùn zhù zìjǐ.
examples.en: Attachment to fame and fortune ultimately only weaves a cocoon around oneself.

examples.zh: 作茧自缚的故事告诉我们，过度的自我保护反而会伤害自己。
examples.pinyin: Zuò jiǎn zì fù de gùshì gàosu wǒmen, guòdù de zìwǒ bǎohù fǎn'ér huì shānghài zìjǐ.
examples.en: The story of cocooning oneself teaches that excessive self-protection ultimately harms oneself.
